references.text: Simon and Andrew left their nets and followed Jesus, just as the disciples in Luke 5:11 left everything and followed him.
James and John left the boat and their father and followed Jesus—the same pattern of leaving all to follow Jesus.
Peter says to Jesus, 'We have left everything and followed you.' This directly summarizes the action described in Luke 5:11.
Simon and Andrew left their nets and followed Jesus, parallel to Luke 5:11 where the disciples leave everything and follow him.
James and John left their father Zebedee in the boat and followed Jesus, a parallel account of leaving all to follow Jesus.
Peter says, 'We have left everything and followed you,' which directly reflects the action in Luke 5:11.
Levi left everything, got up, and followed Jesus—the same expressions 'ἀφέντες πάντα' and 'ἠκολούθησαν' are used for leaving all to follow Jesus.
Jesus says that whoever does not give up all they own cannot be his disciple. This is the theological basis behind the action in 5:11.
Peter says they have left everything they owned and followed Jesus, and Jesus confirms that whoever has left house or family for the sake of God's kingdom will receive much more in return.
Paul counted all things as loss to gain Christ—the same principle of leaving all to follow Christ, as the disciples did in Luke 5:11.
